ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic screening standards: every director, shareholder, UBO, signatory, and commercial counterparty must be screened before incorporation against the New Zealand Consolidated Sanctions List (Sanctions Act 2019), the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Restricted List, and FATF public statements. PEPs require enhanced due diligence and must be escalated to the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit in accordance with section 53 of the AML/CFT Act 2009. A negative screening result may be accepted only after a written risk assessment and sign-off by the AML/CFT compliance officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Company Name Reservation (accessible via the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Portal at www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or Māori using Latin script (A–Z, a–z, 0–9 and limited punctuation marks; macrons in Māori are acceptable). Non-Latin scripts are not accepted for New Zealand company registration. The Registrar applies the similarity-of-names test under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993, including phonetic and visual comparison and loose transliteration into English or Māori.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank (reserved for registered banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021)
Insurance (requires licensing under the Insurance Prudential Supervision Act 2010)
Trust (restricted unless an express trust deed is provided and approved)
University (requires consent of the Ministry of Education)
Anzac (protected under the Anzac Day Act 1995)
Red Cross (protected under the Geneva Conventions Act 2006)
Olympic (restricted under the Olympic Symbol Protection Act 1996)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant receives a written refusal stating the statutory grounds. The applicant may file a written review application with the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days, providing legal and evidentiary submissions. The Registrar must respond within 20 working days. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Senior Courts Act 2016 and the High Court Rules, naming the Registrar as respondent, within 30 days of the final decision. Where the ground is similarity to an existing name, the applicant may obtain the existing company’s written consent and resubmit the reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a digital health/fitness app business only if the registered office is a physical address in New Zealand (not a P.O. Box), is staffed by the company or a licensed registered office provider during ordinary business hours, and is appointed as the agent for service of process. A virtual office using a serviced address may satisfy the Companies Act 1993 and the AML/CFT Act 2009, provided the provider maintains a compliant mail forwarding, record retention, and statutory document inspection facility.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: approximately 10% to 15% annual likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by the Registrar of Companies under section 53 of the Companies Act 1993 or by an AML/CFT supervisor under the AML/CFT Act 2009, reflecting the low-risk, non-licensed, digital telemetry nature of the sector. Likelihood increases to 30% if any adverse UBO index entry or sanctions hit is identified during screening.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 10 (formation by one or more incorporators), 12(1) (obligation to register), 13 (conclusive Certificate of Incorporation), 15 (full legal capacity), 16 (statement of purpose), 25-30 (constitution), 36-47 (shares, capital and solvency certificate), 122-128 (directors' duties, indemnities), 131-138 (good faith and conflicts of interest), 151-152 (director consent; at least one director resident in New Zealand), 185-200 (meetings, registers, records), 211-215 (financial records and annual return); Companies Regulations 1994, regs 3-6; Income Tax Act 2007, ss YD 4 (non-resident company definition), CW 9 (exempt income) and HR 8 (elective tax-exempt classification for the International Company); Financial Reporting Act 2013 (reporting entity thresholds); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (reporting entity scope for corporate services).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the online New Zealand Companies Register (app.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form NZCN1) lodged electronically through the New Zealand Companies Register, resulting in the Registrar's Certificate of Incorporation issued under s 13 of the Companies Act 1993 and the automatic allocation of a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Nil statutory minimum paid-up capital. The International Company may be incorporated with zero issued capital or with nominal share capital; no escrow account, capital deposit, or capital verification requirement applies (ss 36(5) and 37(2), Companies Act 1993). Shares may be denominated in NZD, USD, GBP or EUR, and consideration may be satisfied by cash, promissory note, or in-kind assets, provided that any capital-reduction distribution is supported by a board solvency certificate under s 47. The ELF_CUSTOM_CK_IC tax-exempt model is available regardless of capital amount.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Register – Online Name Availability Search (NZCO/MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an electronic name search on the Companies Register portal to confirm that the proposed name is not identical or almost identical to any existing registered name, reserved name, or registered trademark under the Trade Marks Act 2002 (ss 21-22, Companies Act 1993). Where the name contains restricted words (for example trust, bank, insurance, medical, or national), obtain written consent from the relevant regulator (e.g. the Financial Markets Authority or the Reserve Bank of New Zealand). Submit the proposed name either as a stand-alone reservation (20-working-day hold) or proceed directly to incorporation. The International Company may omit the Limited suffix only if the constitution prohibits domestic trading and the tax-exempt International Company election is made; the standard Limited suffix is nevertheless recommended for treaty and perception purposes.
required_dossiers: Three ranked proposed company names
Completed name availability search results
Consent letters or regulator approvals for restricted words (if applicable)
Identification of the NZ-resident director and ultimate beneficial owners for vetting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as too similar, obtain a signed letter of no-objection from the existing company or trade mark owner and re-file, or select an alternative name. A formal reconsideration may be requested from the NZCO Registrar, and any adverse decision is subject to judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarisation of Constitution and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Notary Public and admitted barrister or solicitor of the High Court of New Zealand (external legal counsel)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the constitution of the International Company in accordance with ss 25-30 of the Companies Act 1993, or adopt the default constitution contained in Schedule 1. For the CK_IC exempt model, include the full statement of purpose (development and operation of fitness biometric tracking and wellness telemetry software, biometric data analytics, cloud hosting, intellectual property licensing, and digital e-commerce), flexible share class and denomination provisions, the director indemnity and insurance clause (s 162), conflict-of-interest wavier, binding arbitration clause, and perpetual succession language. Have the constitution, the Incorporation Application signatures, director consent forms (s 151), and share subscription forms notarised by a New Zealand notary public. If the documents will be used outside New Zealand, obtain an Apostille certificate pursuant to the Oaths and Declarations Act 1957 and the Apostille Convention.
required_dossiers: Two originals of the notarised constitution (or Schedule 1 default adoption notice)
Certified passport copies of all directors and subscribers
Directors Declaration of Consent (Form NZCN2 section) under s 151
Corporate resolutions and powers of attorney of any corporate subscriber
Proof of physical New Zealand address for the resident director and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NZCO queries a constitutional clause as contrary to s 29 (prohibited provisions), amend the offending clause to align with the Companies Act 1993 mandatory protections and re-notarise. If the notary declines certification owing to identity insufficiency, resubmit with newer utility bills, bank references, and valid passports.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgment of Form NZCN1 and Payment of Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the New Zealand Companies Register using a RealMe authenticated account and select the Register a Company service. Complete Form NZCN1 online with the approved company name, physical New Zealand street address for the registered office (a post-office box is invalid), postal address, constitution upload (PDF of the notarised document or adoption of Schedule 1), full legal names, dates of birth and residential addresses of all directors and shareholders, the number and class of shares issued, and confirmation of the single NZ-resident director. Pay the statutory registration fee of NZD 137.50 (including GST, approximately USD 80 at prevailing rates) by debit or credit card. Upon satisfaction of the requirements in s 12(1), the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under s 13, together with an automatic New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), effective as at the time of registration.
required_dossiers: Completed Form NZCN1 database fields
Constitution PDF, notarised if custom-drafted
Written consent of each director (s 151)
Evidence of the physical New Zealand registered office address (lease or title)
Shareholder information including beneficial ownership declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Register issues a notice to provide further information or rejects the application, use the online correction window of five business days to amend the flagged fields and resubmit. For substantive objections, file a written submission with the Registrar of Companies, and if necessary invoke the Companies Office reconsideration procedure; persistent refusal may be challenged by judicial review in the High Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registration with Inland Revenue and AML/CFT Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD); Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) of the New Zealand Police; NZCO (record maintenance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NZBN issued at incorporation, register the company with the IRD through the myIR online portal: (i) confirm the automatically allocated IRD number, (ii) register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) where annual taxable turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 or where voluntary registration is commercially beneficial for input credits, (iii) register for PAYE if employees are engaged in New Zealand, and (iv) file the Notice of Non-Resident Status (Form IR 105) where central management and control is exercised offshore and the company derives predominantly foreign-source income, thereby confirming the tax-exempt classification under the ELF_CUSTOM_CK_IC model. If the International Company itself provides designated services (for example managing or controlling client money or administering gaming/enrolment platforms), register as a reporting entity under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 with the FIU; where a licensed corporate services provider performs these functions, the provider holds the registration.
required_dossiers: NZBN and IRD number confirmation
Certificate of Incorporation (PDF)
Form IR 105 non-resident company declaration (if applicable)
GST and PAYE registration forms
Beneficial ownership register extract (AML/CFT compliance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD classifies the IC as a New Zealand tax resident in error, file Form IR 105 with contemporaneous evidence of offshore central management and control (board minutes, resolutions, meeting locations). If the classification is maintained, issue a Notice of Proposed Adjustment (NOPA) under Part 4A of the Tax Administration Act 1994 within the applicable response window and request an adjudication or binding ruling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Physical Establishment and Statutory Records Custody
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent or corporate secretarial provider (Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand member or NZ-registered professional) and the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Formalise a registered office service agreement with a local licensed provider so that the International Company maintains a genuine New Zealand street address at which legal process may be served (ss 189-190, Companies Act 1993). Establish or transfer the statutory records: certificate of incorporation, constitution, register of members, register of directors' consents, register of directors' interests, share transfer ledger, and minutes of board and shareholder meetings. Comply with s 213 by calendaring the annual return due within one month following the annual incorporation anniversary; failure to file causes the Registrar to initiate strike-off proceedings. For the tax-exempt International Company, additionally maintain an income-source schedule and double tax agreement analysis supporting the offshore exemption claim.
required_dossiers: Registered office service agreement (physical street address)
Company minute book and statutory registers
Directors' service and remuneration agreements
Annual return calendar configuration in the Companies Register
Shareholder and director change log templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Register flags an overdue annual return or incomplete director information, utilise the online make-annual-return function immediately. If the company has already been struck off under s 120, apply for reinstatement to the Registrar within two years, or obtain a High Court reinstatement order under s 121.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Cook Islands Ministry of Finance and Economic Management – Revenue Management Division (RMD) in association with the Cook Islands Financial Services Development Authority (FSDA) for International Company registration; official portal: www.mfem.gov.ck / www.fsda.gov.ck. As the Cook Islands is a self-governing territory in free association with New Zealand, the New Zealand Inland Revenue Department (IRD) (www.ird.govt.nz) is the sovereign-level revenue authority but asserts no taxing jurisdiction over a Cook Islands International Company unless a New Zealand permanent establishment, GST nexus, or remote-services supply obligation is established.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the CK_IC under the International Companies Act 2012 through a licensed international company service provider at the FSDA Companies Registry, filing the Memorandum and Articles of Association and appointing a registered agent and registered office in Rarotonga. Step 2: Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and the statutory Certificate of Tax Exemption confirming the entity's exempt status under Section 120 of the International Companies Act 2012. Step 3: Apply to the Revenue Management Division for a Cook Islands VAT registration number (RMD VAT ID) only if actual or projected annual taxable turnover of non-exempt local supplies exceeds NZD 30,000; a wholly offshore digital application business is ordinarily not registrable. Step 4: Where the entity establishes a New Zealand taxable nexus outside the Apple/Google marketplace framework, apply to the New Zealand IRD for an overseas company IRD number via the myIR portal using the non-resident company registration application (IR742), and separately register for GST if annual NZ taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — A Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) is a resident company of the Cook Islands but enjoys a statutory exemption from all Cook Islands income tax, asset transfer duty, stamp duty, capital gains tax, and exchange control in respect of all income and activities carried on outside the Cook Islands. The entity is therefore not subject to entity-level taxation on offshore health/fitness application revenue; this is a categorical offshore exemption (Corporate Tax Exempt Zone) rather than a pass-through election, and the exemption does not extend to any business carried on within the Cook Islands with domestic customers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The International Companies Act 2012 permits the CK_IC to elect in its constitutive documents to adopt the status of a non-resident company for exchange-control and stamp-duty purposes, to migrate from the repealed International Companies Act 1981-82 by written election filed with the FSDA, and to elect to contract out of default share capital and board quorum provisions. No US-style check-the-box or OECD hybrid-mismatch election exists in Cook Islands law; the New Zealand Income Tax Act 2007 branch and GST elections (including the elective filing of consolidated GST returns and the s HG 4 group company election) are available only where a New Zealand PE or taxable presence is separately created, and their use does not derogate from the Cook Islands tax exemption.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Cook Islands Value Added Tax Act 2012, administered by the Revenue Management Division; the New Zealand Goods and Services Tax (GST) Act 1985 applies exclusively where the entity establishes a New Zealand taxable nexus, and for app-store sales the electronic marketplace operator (Apple App Store / Google Play) is the statutory supplier responsible for collecting and remitting GST/VAT in the consumer-market jurisdictions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Cook Islands VAT: NZD 30,000 annual taxable turnover of domestic taxable supplies; New Zealand GST: NZD 60,000 annual taxable supplies (remote services and digital marketplace supplies sold via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing are subject to the marketplace operator's registration obligations, not the CK_IC's, under the NZ GST (Remote Services) and marketplace rules)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Cook Islands: no real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing, or digital stamping mandate exists; VAT invoices must be issued within one month of the supply and retained for six years, with VAT returns filed electronically through the RMD portal by the 28th day of the month following the taxable period. New Zealand: voluntary Peppol-based NZ e-Invoicing framework aligned with Peppol BIS 3.0 only; no mandatory e-invoicing or pre-clearance. Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console generated financial reports and country-specific tax summary statements serve as the primary transactional evidence for app revenue, replacing conventional paper invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% VAT under the Cook Islands VAT Act 2012 applies to (i) the export of goods, and (ii) services supplied to a recipient outside the Cook Islands at the time of supply, including digital health/fitness app subscriptions, biometric telemetry processing, and licensing transactions undertaken by the CK_IC with non-resident counterparties. For supplies via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, the zero-rating classification rests on the supply by the CK_IC to the offshore marketplace operator (Apple Inc. / Google LLC) together with the digital platform's arm's-length settlement, supported by evidence of non-resident status (app-store transaction geo-location, foreign card billing addresses, and platform-sourced analytics) and by a written service/licence agreement showing the performance of all activities outside the Cook Islands. The supply must not involve any domestic Cook Islands consumer and must not be physically performed within the Cook Islands.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (where physical goods are involved) or digital service export declaration for the Revenue Management Division

Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of goods, alternatively the Apple App Store Connect / Google Play Console settlement report and end-user licence agreement evidencing the offshore digital supply
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice from the CK_IC's licensed international bank account evidencing receipt of the foreign-currency app-store settlement proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to retrospective audit by the Cook Islands Revenue Management Division for a period of six years from the end of the tax period in which the supply was reported. Where substantiation is deficient or the export claim is established as fraudulent, the entity is liable to clawback of the unremitted 15% VAT on the gross supply value, a late-payment penalty of 10% of the tax shortfall, and statutory interest at the prescribed rate prevailing in the Cook Islands. Knowingly false zero-rating declarations constitute an offence under Part 8 of the VAT Act 2012, punishable by fine and imprisonment of up to five years, and the FSDA may revoke the International Company's Certificate of Tax Exemption. Where a separate New Zealand GST registration exists, the New Zealand Tax Administration Act 1994 shortfall penalties apply on a scale of 20% (not taking reasonable care) to 150% (abusive tax avoidance), with criminal liability for evasion of tax under section 143A.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) — the statutory prudential regulator of all licensed banks under the Cook Islands Banking Act 2009. The Cook Islands has no separate central bank and no domestic paper currency; monetary authority functions are exercised by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) as issuer of the New Zealand Dollar, which is the sole legal tender of the Cook Islands. The Cook Islands Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM) oversees national financial-sector policy, and the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) is the AML/CFT regulator for transaction monitoring and suspicious-activity reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Cook Islands maintains no exchange-control regime and the New Zealand Dollar is fully and freely convertible. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are liberalised: (i) current-account flows — Apple IAP and Google Play Billing net settlements in USD, cloud-services payments, software-licence fees, contractor disbursements — require no central-bank approval; (ii) capital-account flows — share-subscription injections, shareholder loans, intercompany funding, and dividend distributions — are unrestricted and require no prior licence, approval, or registration with the FSC or MFEM. Profit remittance by a Cook Islands International Company (IC) is entirely unfettered: under the International Companies Act 1981-82 (Cook Islands), an IC that does not carry on business in the Cook Islands is exempt from income tax, withholding tax, capital-gains tax, and stamp duty; therefore dividends, management fees, interest, and liquidation proceeds may be remitted to non-resident shareholders and creditors without deduction of any Cook Islands tax. The sole practical hurdle is not regulatory but banking-compliance-driven: the company must evidence its tax-exempt certificate, its registered-agent status in Rarotonga, and the lawful commercial substance of its ISIC 6201 digital-health and fitness telemetry operations to satisfy bank due-diligence and correspondent-bank clearance standards.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, conversion, or repatriation requirement applies to export proceeds earned by a Cook Islands International Company. The full amount of foreign-currency receipts — including USD/EUR settlements from Apple and Google app-store sales — may be retained indefinitely in designated foreign-currency accounts without mandatory conversion into NZD, without any prescribed holding timeline, and with no minimum surrender ratio. The company is free to operate a multi-currency treasury (USD, NZD, EUR, or HKD) and to convert balances at market-determined rates for operational funding, hedging, or dividend distribution purposes, subject only to the bank's internal account-activity policy and the economic-substance description in the board-approved business plan.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Treasury Account — multi-currency current accounts (USD and NZD) with SWIFT direct membership and online dealing desk; segregated Capital Escrow Account for issued-share capital and shareholder-loan escrow where proceeds are held pending share-certificate issuance

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (Cook Islands) Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account — NZD/USD transaction account with term-deposit sweep; Capital Escrow Account (trust-backed) available for subscription funds pending UBO verification

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of the Cook Islands Limited (BCI)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account — domestic NZD-denominated account only; does not support the foreign-currency, SWIFT/correspondent and treasury-hedging requirements of an offshore International Company

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: LOW (direct on-boarding for a Cook Islands-domiciled International Company); MEDIUM-HIGH (indirect via a New Zealand operating subsidiary or branch). Global digital EMIs — including Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, Revolut Business, and Stripe Treasury — generally decline to on-board a company incorporated in the Cook Islands because of the jurisdiction's residual offshore-centre risk profile, periodic FATF/EU monitoring history, and the thin correspondent-bank appetite for Cook Islands BIC/routing prefixes. Direct EMI account opening in the name of the CK IC should be treated as unavailable unless the specific EMI's compliance department confirms acceptance in writing. The legally compliant and operationally effective alternative is to interpose a New Zealand-registered operating company (the app vendor and merchant of record) that holds the EMI and Apple/Google merchant accounts, with back-to-back intercompany service agreements upstream to the CK IC for IP licensing and a documented transfer-pricing policy. This preserves the tax-exempt IC structure while allowing access to modern payment infrastructure and low-cost FX conversion.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for at least one director and the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO). ANZ Bank (Cook Islands) Limited and Bank of South Pacific (Cook Islands) Limited require an in-person KYC interview at the Rarotonga branch (or, at the bank's sole discretion, at a designated ANZ/BSP office in Auckland facilitated by the New Zealand affiliate) before account activation. Remote-only onboarding is not offered for a tax-exempt offshore International Company; the only permitted relaxation is a hybrid video interview for additional directors or for a director located outside the Pacific, provided: (i) the Cook Islands licensed registered agent physically attends the interview at the bank; (ii) the director's passport and proof-of-address are certified by a notary or by a bank officer in the director's location with a banker's letter confirming verification; and (iii) the bank's compliance committee approves the video waiver in writing. The onboarding package must be pre-cleared by the registered agent, and all corporate seals, apostilled board resolutions, and shareholder documents must be lodged at least seven business days before the interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore Tax-Exempt IC Characterisation — the bank's initial screening flags the CK IC as a potential tax-evasion or money-laundering conduit because of its zero-tax status, non-resident directors, and intangible-only digital-health business model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Certificate of Incorporation and the tax-exemption certificate issued under the International Companies Act 1981-82; (ii) current Certificate of Good Standing from the Cook Islands Registry; (iii) complete shareholder register and UBO declaration identifying all natural persons; (iv) notarised board resolution confirming the lawful ISIC 6201 activity; (v) executed Apple Developer Program Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement evidencing the in-app-purchase revenue stream; (vi) certified passports, proof-of-address (utility/bank statements), and professional reference letters for each director and UBO; (vii) a board-approved three-year business plan with revenue, expense, and treasury flow forecasts for the fitness-biometric tracking application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance and Anchoring Default — the IC has no staff, no office, and no contract with a local employer in Rarotonga, and the name/targeting overlay suggests a captive or asset-holding vehicle with no real operational footprint, triggering enhanced due-diligence or refusal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Cook Islands substance folder: registered-agent agreement, local corporate-services certificate, registered-office address, and the IC's statutory records kept at the Rarotonga office; (ii) New Zealand substance dossier: software-development lease/office in NZ, employment contracts for the engineering and data-science team, payroll records, ACC and GST registration for the NZ operating entity, evidencing that the app is actually designed, developed, and supported in the NZ/Cook Islands corridor; (iii) group structure chart with the CK IC as IP owner and the NZ entity as app developer and merchant of record; (iv) executed licensing and development service agreements between the CK IC and the NZ operating company with arm's-length pricing; (v) annual economic-substance return (where applicable under the Cook Islands substance framework) declaring the IP-holding and financing activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactional Velocity Anomaly — thousands of USD/EUR Apple/Google micro-payments credited to a single corporate account, combined with rapid onward payments to contractors and service providers, triggers transaction-monitoring alerts and potential Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) escalation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Monthly merchant-payout statements from Apple and Google, reconciling gross billings, platform commissions (15-30%), FX conversion rates, and net settlement amounts to the bank account; (ii) certified privacy/security framework documentation for the health app (ISO/IEC 27001 attestation, SOC 2 report, and GDPR/CCTA compliance evidence) demonstrating regulated, institutional provenance of the payment stream; (iii) detailed contractor payment register with invoices, contracts, and corporate identification for each recipient; (iv) signed treasury policy mandating separate operating and escrow accounts, weekly batching of intercompany transfers, and documented FX forward/NDF tickets for all USD-NZD conversions; (v) monthly CFO treasury pack with cash-flow waterfall, entered into the bank's digital portal on a standing instruction basis; (vi) letter from the Cook Islands FSC or MFEM confirming nil domestic tax liability on app receipts, so that the bank cannot book an unexplained tax-discrepancy alert.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Correspondent-Bank Rejection at the USD Clearing Layer — upstream US and Australian correspondent banks refuse to clear USD-denominated wire transfers bearing the Cook Islands beneficiary bank BIC or jurisdiction routing prefix, citing historical grey-list and offshore-centre policy.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Direct account relationship with a licensed NZ clearing bank (ANZ NZ, ASB, or Westpac NZ) that maintains strong US correspondent lines, and the instruction to route all USD by MT103 via the NZ bank's RMBK/CHIPS-cleared account, avoiding CKD-prefixed SWIFT routing; (ii) executed W-8BEN-E (FATCA) and CRS self-certification for the CK IC, confirming non-US status and full tax-reporting compliance; (iii) annual external AML/CFT audit of the CK IC and its NZ operating entity performed by a Big-4 firm, aligned with the Cook Islands AML/CFT Act 2004 and FSC Guidelines; (iv) beneficial-ownership attestation signed by all controllers confirming no Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are connected; (v) board-approved treasury policy committing to NZ-cleared USD rails, demonstrating that the structure is designed to mitigate, rather than evade, correspondent-bank compliance vetting.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for the initial subscription of issued share capital and/or shareholder loans into the CK IC (ISIC 6201 app development funding): (i) settle via SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the shareholder's bank to the beneficiary account held at ANZ Bank (Cook Islands) Limited or Bank of South Pacific (Cook Islands) Limited; (ii) use ISO 20022 purpose codes 'EQUI' for paid-up capital and 'DEBT'/'INTR' for shareholder loans, and state in SWIFT Field 70: 'Subscription for ordinary shares of CK IC per board resolution dated [date]' or 'Intercompany shareholder loan for ISIC 6201 fitness-telemetry software development'; (iii) before remittance, the recipient bank must hold an executed Capitalisation Letter from the Cook Islands registered agent, a board resolution specifying share-count and share premium, and source-of-wealth documentation for the remitting shareholder; (iv) for any transaction passing through New Zealand, confirm that the Overseas Investment Act 2005 exemption applies — the CK IC is not acquiring 'sensitive New Zealand assets' in the ordinary course of capital injection, and no OIA consent is required; (v) funds above NZD 50,000 trigger an automatic request for the substance dossier described in the KYC defence section, so the dossier should be pre-positioned with the bank; (vi) grant destination: a segregated Capital Escrow Account in the IC's name; the funds may be moved to the operating account only after the share registers are updated, share certificates issued, and the bank's compliance officer releases the escrow ledger. For CRS/FATCA purposes the bank will record the payer's tax residence; the shareholder must provide W-8BEN/W-9 and CRS self-certification at the onboarding stage.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement rails are standard SWIFT-based and documentary-trade compliant: (i) ordinary operational disbursements — cloud-infrastructure fees (AWS Sydney), software licences, contractor fees, and marketing payments — are executed by SWIFT MT103 with purpose-coded narratives ('SOFT', 'CLDS', 'CNTR', 'MARK'); (ii) any high-value or credit-sensitive trade settlement can additionally be effected by Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) with the CK IC as applicant at the Rarotonga bank and the beneficiary's bank confirming; the documentary package (commercial invoice, electronic delivery receipt, inspection certificate where agreed) must be presented through the Swiss-API or documentary-collection desk of the issuing bank; (iii) intra-group funding to the New Zealand operating company should be batched weekly rather than daily to minimise transaction-monitoring noise, and classified as intercompany loan/services under the transfer-pricing policy; (iv) dividend distributions and loan repayments to non-resident shareholders are processed free of any Cook Islands withholding tax, but must be evidenced by a board-approved solvency certificate, an updated register of members, and minutes recording the declaration date; the MT103 narrative should read 'Final dividend for FY[year] declared under International Companies Act [date]' to prevent the receiving bank from re-characterising the flow as taxable service income; (v) all outbound payments must be covered by the annual internal AML/CFT audit trail and reconciled against board-approved budgets to preserve the 'Low-Risk Standard' banking tier.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards (delivery-based USD/NZD and EUR/NZD contracts) with licensed counterparties — ANZ (CKI), BSP (CKI), or a top-25 New Zealand bank — executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and FX Annex, restricted to hedging forecasted app-store USD proceeds into the NZD operating currency for the rolling 12-month treasury forecast

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) — defensively permitted for Asia-Pacific exotic currencies (USD/PHP, USD/IDR, USD/THB) where the CK IC's contractor payments or regional marketing settlements face local convertibility restrictions; NDF trading is channelled through an NZ-regulated derivatives broker subject to the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, with the CK IC documented as an 'eligible investor' for OTC derivatives

Cross-Currency Swaps (USD/NZD and EUR/NZD) — available for balance-sheet hedging of long-term shareholder loans and the Capital Escrow layer, contracted under ISDA 2002 with credit support annex, and designated for hedge accounting under IFRS 9/FRS 14 with documented hedge-effectiveness testing by the group treasury manager

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 working days after the anniversary of incorporation, as notified by the Companies Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may trigger a Notice of Intention to Remove under Companies Act 1993 s 318; persistent non-filing for two or more annual returns can lead to administrative striking-off, director disqualification, and loss of corporate legal capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial statements and auditor's report, if audit threshold is triggered or shareholders do not unanimously waive audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; where required, Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be signed and dated within 5 months of the balance date; if required to be filed, filed within 20 working days after signature
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, exposing the company and directors to financial penalties and director liability; persistent failure may be ground for removal from the register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit applies to FMC reporting entities and large companies. A company is large if it satisfies at least two of: total assets exceed NZD 60 million; total revenue exceeds NZD 30 million; more than 50 employees. A non-large, non-FMC company may avoid audit if all shareholders agree in writing.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial Reporting Act 2013 and XRB A1 framework; entities must apply NZ IFRS (with Tier 2 reduced-disclosure relief available) or the XRB-approved simplified accounting framework for small non-publicly-accountable entities; tax-basis accounts may be required separately by Inland Revenue.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not require a separate annual UBO filing. The annual return confirms current directors and shareholders at the anniversary date; any share transfers during the year must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the next annual return. AML/CFT-regulated service providers must verify beneficial ownership through customer due diligence, but beneficial-owner information is not filed with the Companies Office.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200–600 per annum for a registered office and corporate agent in a standard New Zealand company secretarial retainer
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–12,000 per engagement for a small to mid-sized technology company; nil where the audit is validly waived and no threshold is met

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays. R&D tax credit at 15% of eligible expenditure; deduction for clinical trial expenditure (150%); depreciation on digital app development assets per IRD rules; no preferential IP box regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically via myIR (IRD online portal) or approved software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 7th day of the 7th month after balance date (e.g., 31 March balance date: due 7 October); extended deadlines apply for agents with terminal tax dates

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, IRD number, and registered address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the New Zealand registered office address and IRD number as registered by the non-resident company
Include New Zealand-source income only unless treaty and PE rules require broader apportionment; attach disclosure of foreign income if a New Zealand tax resident for treaty purposes
Claim deductible expenses incurred in deriving New Zealand-source income; apportion head office costs strictly in accordance with transfer pricing and IRD administrative guidelines
Compute New Zealand taxable income after deducting allowable expenses; non-resident companies are taxed only on New Zealand-source income attributable to a fixed establishment or PE
Non-resident companies without ICA must disclose NIL; attach a note explaining no New Zealand-resident shareholders and no imputation credits
Calculate tax on net taxable income at 28%; claim treaty credit for any foreign tax if applicable
Only claim if the non-resident has a New Zealand PE and eligible R&D is performed in New Zealand; attach IRD approval and expenditure breakdown
Non-resident companies may carry forward losses under continuity rules (49% continuity for same business); attach shareholder continuity schedule

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: NZ$250 initial, plus NZ$50 for each further month of non-filing. Late payment penalty: 1% of unpaid tax immediately, then 1.5% per month thereafter. Use-of-money interest applies on unpaid tax at IRD prescribed rates (currently 9.91% for underpayments as of 2025).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% on gross dividends paid to non-residents (non-resident withholding tax, NRWT)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident must: (1) be a tax resident of the treaty jurisdiction; (2) obtain a Certificate of Residence (CoR) from the foreign tax authority; (3) provide the CoR to the New Zealand payer or complete form IR67 (Certificate of Exemption from NRWT) prior to payment; (4) where treaty rate is lower (e.g., 15% under NZ–China DTA, 5% for 10%+ shareholding), payer may apply the reduced rate with an approved certificate; refund applications via IRD for excess NRWT deducted must be lodged within 4 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 15% (Approved Issuer Levy not available); treaty rates vary (NZ–USA 5%, NZ–UK 10%, NZ–China 10%) subject to beneficial ownership and limitation-on-benefits. Interest: statutory 15%; most treaties reduce to 0-10% (NZ–USA 0%, NZ–UK 10%, NZ–China 10%); Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% applies to certain offshore related-party interest if conditions met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: NZ$10 million (approx. USD 6.3M) related-party cross-border transactions; Master File: NZ$50 million (approx. USD 31.5M) group revenue threshold; Country-by-Country Report: NZ$1.14 billion group revenue threshold (OECD threshold as adopted).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand applies general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR, s BG1 Income Tax Act 2007) and transfer pricing rules under s GC 13-GC 15, aligning with OECD TP Guidelines. No separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as in Cayman/BVI; however, the IRD will scrutinise substance through PE attribution, beneficial ownership, anti-conduit rules, and thin capitalisation. For a digital health app tracker, functional analysis must demonstrate that software development, data hosting, user contracts, and risk management are performed where the economic substance resides.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of New Zealand-source digital subscription revenue from health app sales to New Zealand users; failing to register for GST when supplies exceed NZ$60,000; hiding beneficial ownership of the International Company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Tax Administration Act 1994 s 143A and s 143B: strict liability penalty of 75% of the evaded tax for abusive tax position; evasion offence punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and/or fine up to NZ$50,000 (individual) or NZ$250,000 (company); asset restraining orders and confiscation under Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly assist in evasion are personally liable for the company's unpaid tax via PAYE/GST director penalty notices (s 166 of Tax Administration Act 1994); civil restoration of funds; travel bans available under the Insolvency Act 2006; extradition to New Zealand possible under bilateral treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging inflated royalties or service fees from the New Zealand PE to the offshore International Company to erode New Zealand taxable profits; absence of contemporaneous TP documentation for app IP licensing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRD recharacterisation and adjustment of taxable income; shortfall penalty of 20% for unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross lack of reasonable care, 100% for evasion; interest on unpaid tax at 9.91% p.a.; denial of deductions for non-arm's length payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be made jointly and severally liable for TP shortfall penalties if they knowingly participate in arrangements lacking commercial rationale; personal liability orders under Companies Act 1993 for reckless trading; director disqualification orders up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: International Company with no physical presence, no employees, and no active decision-making in New Zealand, while contracting with app developers in third countries and deriving revenue from New Zealand users without filing tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of the entity as having a New Zealand PE; taxation of all New Zealand-source income at 28%; imposition of NRWT and RWT obligations; penalties for failure to register with the Companies Office (NZ$500 per month) plus late filing penalties; possible strike-off and deregistration under Companies Act 1993.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell company face civil liability for unpaid taxes and penalties; New Zealand courts may pierce the corporate veil where the company is a mere façade; directors may face arrest on warrant for failure to pay fines, travel bans under the Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters Act, and bans on managing companies for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting customer subscription payments via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing without implementing AML/CFT compliance controls, customer due diligence, and transaction monitoring; using anonymous prepaid cards or crypto to obscure revenue flows from fitness app users
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act): civil penalties up to NZ$1.1 million for entities and NZ$220,000 for individuals per breach; criminal penalties up to NZ$2 million and imprisonment up to 2 years for directors; court-ordered disclosure and freezing orders under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for AML/CFT compliance failures where they directed or acquiesced in the breach; the FMA and Department of Internal Affairs can issue infringement notices and seek disqualification; individuals may be prohibited from managing a financial services company for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register and charge New Zealand GST (15%) on digital services supplied to New Zealand consumers where the company is a non-resident supplier with NZ$60,000 or more annual supplies; failing to file GST returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalty NZ$250 plus NZ$50 per month; late payment penalty 1% plus 1.5% monthly; use-of-money interest; measures: GST evasion offence under Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 s 144B: imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to NZ$50,000; director penalty notices under s 183G.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid GST via director penalty notice if they fail to ensure GST is deducted when due; personal bankruptcy proceedings possible for directors who continue to trade while insolvent; travel restrictions and statutory demands.
